name: Balz
prior: Friction drum physics is published, not shipped: Onofrei, Willemsen & Serafin, 'Real-Time Implementation of a Friction Drum Inspired Instrument Using Finite Difference Schemes' (DAFx20in21) - bowed membrane + 1D tube, elasto-plastic friction, movable excitation point, played from a Sensel Morph [VS: vbn.aau.dk DAFx20in21_paper_32.pdf; dafx.de archive]; Willemsen/Bilbao/Serafin elasto-plastic bowed stiff string < 6% CPU (DAFx 2019) [VS: vbn.aau.dk DAFx2019Willemsen.pdf]; IRCAM Modalys for Max (real-time; bow connection on strings, force connection on membranes, bowed membrane not documented) [VS: support.ircam.fr Modalys 3.8.0; forum.ircam.fr tutorial 5]; Mutable Elements bows modal resonators (hardware, no membrane mode set) [A]; nlm Max externals do nonlinear membranes but struck [VS: arxiv 2603.10240]; SuperCollider MCLDUGens Friction (single mass on belt) [VS: plugin.sccode.org/MCLDUGens/Help/Friction.html]. Cuica/lion's roar in software: GM drum-kit samples only [VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuíca]; no plugin, app or Eurorack module found in 2 searches (1 extended). In Myzel: no friction in any of the 14 engines; inventor Harz (bowed glass/bowl/bar) is the sibling and shares the bow table.
costNotes: 5 complex resonators ~0.17 [R: webaudio.md s4, 0.034 each]; bow table lookup instead of pow() ~3 ns; stick inertia/random walk per block ~0; the 'Einpol-Formant' must be a 2-pole SVF to be a formant (~12 ns in locals) 0.1; tanh table 0.02; node 0.06 + 3-4 k-rate params 0.1. L1 ~0.5 (idea 0.45, fine). L3 8 modes + Helmholtz + shell + L/R doublets ~0.85. Band-limited noise for the slip zone from the shared NOISE table. Cheapest engine of the four; could share the myzel-bow processor with Harz via a mode-set option (one registration, less module code).
soundHeld: Held is the point: stick-slip on a few inharmonic modes with the hand (y) bending f_k by up to +480 ct and shortening T60 gives the cuica's whoop; the 2-pole formant sweep makes it vocal. Two honest warnings. First, a bow table on a modal bank (the Elements/BandedWG approach) locks onto the lowest mode and produces a reedy, slightly squeaky self-oscillation - more 'balloon rubbed' than 'lion' unless the slip noise and inharmonic (0,n)/(1,n) modes are mixed in audibly; the Aalborg paper needed an elasto-plastic (hysteretic) model for realism. Second, 'laughing' comes entirely from the stroke random walk (direction reversal every 0.5-1.5 s): on a long held chord every voice reverses at its own rate - great for ambient, but a player cannot phrase it; make stroke rate follow vel and Gestik tilt, with the random walk only as default. Pitch is carried by mode (0,1) so column pitch and Bebung work; chords are rough (inharmonic + beating) - a feature for this instrument.
soundBurst: Strong: a short stroke is exactly the cuica 'ha!' and a long gate 'haaa' - the slip onset chirp is the instrument's signature, and Puls density = laughter is a real play idea. Failure: the stick-slip needs ~15-40 ms to lock in; at gates < 20 ms the hit is a dull thud (ok, but then it is just a soft Membran). Level jumps between stroke directions and between slip/stick need the tanh + Membran peak reference (0.62) the idea names; add a slow AGC on the formant output so 'Bruellen' does not clip the voice bus.
failureModes: Stick-slip on 5 low-Q modes tips into permanent slip (continuous noise) at high pressure; limit slope, add slip noise, and scale bow force with y so the hand controls bite
Reedy/squeaky self-oscillation (Elements-style) instead of a voice; needs hysteresis or at least a velocity-dependent friction curve plus the formant to read as animal
One-pole 'formant' is not a formant; use a 2-pole SVF (600-1800 Hz, Q 3-6) swept by y
Bending f_k per block (+480 ct) zippers under fast Hand moves; lerp per sample (planned)
Phrasing: direction reversals are random, not played; map stroke direction/rate to vel/tilt so the Puls and Gestik can shape the laugh
Chords of many inharmonic self-oscillators beat chaotically and sum loud; per-engine polyphony cap (4) and tanh on the sum
Overlap with inventor Harz (same bow table, modal bank): if both ship, the library needs a clear split (Harz = glass/bowl/bar tones, Balz = Fell + Hand + voice)
verdict: Rare: a friction drum physical model exists as an academic FDTD instrument (Aalborg, Sensel Morph) and bowed modal resonators exist in Elements and Modalys, but no plugin, app or module plays a cuica or lion's roar, and nothing puts the hand-as-formant pitch bend on a touch axis. Feasible and the cheapest of the four at about 0.5 units (0.85 at level 3), sharing the bow table with Harz. Held drones and Puls 'ha!' hits will both be distinctive provided the formant is a real 2-pole and the stroke is playable (vel/tilt), not only a random walk; the main risk is that a bow table on five low-Q modes sounds like a rubbed balloon rather than an animal. Build it, after Harz's bow code exists.
